Fixed in 2857769e. Verified against the pinned corpus: ground-truth disagreements 51 -> 49, cve::cve-2025-61727 now correctly rejected, nothing newly broken.

Two testcases flipped, both of this shape:
  cve::cve-2025-61727
  rfc5280::nc::nc-forbids-dnsname-wildcard-san

Correction to this bead's description, which was wrong on one point. It claimed both CVE variants passed. Only the exclusion one did: cve-2025-61727-nc-permits-variant was already rejected with 'name constraints violated at certificate index 0'. CheckMode::Permitted tests containment, so a wildcard SAN not itself within a permitted subtree already fails matches_dns_name -- the gap existed only on the exclusion side, where the test is intersection rather than containment. That made the fix narrower than the recommendation in this bead, and the permitted side needed no change at all.

Implemented the recommended approach -- bound the wildcard's coverage, not its spelling -- and it turned out to be exact rather than defensive-approximate. '*.D' replaces exactly one label, so it stands for {<label>.D}, and that set meets the subtree rooted at E in only two ways: D lies within E, which makes '*.D' a strict subdomain of E as a string and was already caught, or E is itself <one label>.D, which is the only case added. A deeper exclusion such as foo.bar.example.com is unreachable because the wildcard cannot cross a label boundary, and a leading-period exclusion covers only strict subdomains of its apex. Five unit tests in tests_constraint_forms cover the CVE shape and each case that must stay permitted.

The wildcard shape test mirrors pkix-identity's matches_dns_san exactly rather than approximating it, since a spelling that matcher refuses authenticates nothing and one it accepts must be bounded here; any disagreement would be either a refusal of a harmless certificate or another hole of the same shape.

pkix-path bumped 0.4.7 -> 0.4.8, patch level as the behavioural CRL-ordering fix in pkix-revocation-http was. Divergence gate exits 0. Published crates still carry the vulnerable 0.4.7; 0.4.8 is committed but NOT yet published.

Accepted consequence: this is stricter than RFC 5280 read literally. A CA with a narrow dNSName constraint that issues wildcard SANs is now refused.

Adjacent case NOT addressed, flagged rather than claimed: verify_dns_name_with_cn_fallback matches a CN through the same wildcard matcher, and name constraints never examine the CN as a dNSName. A CA excluded from bar.example.com could in principle issue CN=*.example.com with no SAN and authenticate bar.example.com -- but only via the SMTP DANE path (RFC 7672 §3.2.3) and only in DANE-TA mode, where a CA chain is in play at all. Reachability untraced.
